newsitem.title: USA: Samsonite profits on strong sales despite charge.
newsitem.headline: Samsonite profits on strong sales despite charge.

text.p: Samsonite Corp. Monday reported a third-quarter profit as strong sales of the company's Samsonite, American Tourister and Lark luggage and business cases offset a large restructuring charge.

The Denver-based company had profits of $3.4 million, or 22 cents a share, in the quarter ended Oct. 31, compared with a net loss of $11.4 million, or 72 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales rose 13 percent to a record $203.8 million from $180.3 million.
The results include a previously announced $10.7 million charge to restructure corporate operations and one-time costs of $1.8 million to facilitate the restructuring and recent management changes.
Samsonite said product demand was growing stronger for all its brands, both domestically and internationally, with record sales worldwide far exceeding the industry's growth rate.

U.S. sales rose 18 percent from the 1995 third quarter and all three of Samsonite's brands are beginning to benefit from the introduction of EZ Cart upright luggage with four wheels, the company said. European sales grew 14 percent with higher profit margins over the year.
Samsonite said it completed a global price hike in October, which would improve future profits.
The company said it was starting to benefit from the initial implementation of a five-point series of strategies, including operational and marketing actions, developed in May.

"The restructuring...is helping us achieve a more streamlined and responsive organisation, as well as significant cost efficiencies translating to annualized pre-tax savings of about $12.7 million," said Chief Executive Richard Nicolosi.
"The full impact of the expected cost savings should be realised in fiscal periods commencing after November 1997."
Samsonite's stock rose $1.25 to $37.50 on Nasdaq.
